title: Checkpoint load trace / header inspection (scratchpad)
content:
Quick personal breadcrumbs while debugging the weird model load failures seen on dedicated nodes (cluster-dedicated-2a). Mostly commands run, raw error snippets and hypotheses. Keep this as a short lab notebook that I can paste into a ticket (INF-4321) and into a PR description later.

Observed symptom:
- On a small subset of checkpoints uploaded to GCS, the serving runtime raises an immediate error on startup: "ValueError: Unsupported checkpoint header version: 0x0f" or alternately "Checksum mismatch reading shard manifest". These uploads are from the same training pipeline as successful checkpoints, same model size (7B). Only ~6% of uploads fail.

Commands & quick checks run (timestamps local):
- gsutil ls -l gs://redwood-checkpoints/experiment-2025-11-15/ | grep chkpt-20251115-.*
- gsutil cp gs://redwood-checkpoints/experiment-2025-11-15/chkpt-20251115-04.tar.gz /tmp/
- sha256sum /tmp/chkpt-20251115-04.tar.gz  # returned 7a6f... (mismatch vs manifest: expected 3f2b...)
- gunzip -c /tmp/chkpt-20251115-04.tar.gz | tar -tvf -  # tar lists files, but last file timed out when streaming, truncated?
- hexdump -C -n 256 /tmp/chkpt-20251115-04.tar.gz | head -n 40  # header bytes looked unusual at offset 0x40
- python -c "import struct,sys; b=open('/tmp/chkpt-20251115-04.tar.gz','rb').read(64); print(b.hex())"  # print raw header hex
- dd if=/tmp/chkpt-20251115-04.tar.gz bs=1 skip=512 count=64 | hexdump -C  # inspect potential embedded metadata at 512B
- gsutil cp worked on node-A but failed on node-B intermittently (transient network?), retried with -n to avoid overwrite

Runtime logs (redacted):
- 2026-01-28T03:12:11Z ERROR serving.runtime.checkpoint Loader: Exception reading checkpoint header: ValueError('Unsupported checkpoint header version: 0x0f')
- 2026-01-28T03:12:11Z DEBUG serving.runtime.checkpoint header_bytes: "0a 3c 00 ff 10 00 00 00 7f 45 4c 46 ..."
- 2026-01-28T03:12:11Z ERROR serving.runtime.checkpoint manifest verification failed: computed sha256 != manifest.sha256

Partial hypothesis list (brainstorm):
1) Upload pipeline occasionally applies an extra layer of compression (zstd vs gzip) -> magic bytes differ and header parser mis-detects version.
2) Some training shards include an extra sentinel block at the start (training sampler metadata) which moves expected offsets. The runtime expects header at offset 0 and fails when sentinel present.
3) Endianness or struct packing mismatch from a specific trainer binary when run on an ARM builder (we had an ARM spot-run for experiment-2025-11-15).
4) Manifest uploaded by process A while tarball still being written (race). Manifest recorded sha256 of complete file but object reflects partial/streamed write due to eventual consistency; leads to checksum mismatch at load.
5) GCS transfer corruption (rare) or multi-part upload semantics with concurrent rewrites.

Evidence collected for each hypothesis:
- (1) Magic bytes: checked first 4 bytes across 10 failing vs 10 passing files. Passing consistently start with 1f 8b (gzip); failing set had some with 28 b5 2f 5d (likely zstd or a different container).
- (2) For one failing file I extracted the first 1024 bytes and saw a small ASCII chunk: "SENTINEL:shard_meta v2 -- builder:trainer-3"; this is not present in passing files. Suggests training binary appended preface.
- (3) Build logs: experiment-2025-11-15 used spot-run node type aarch64-small for chunking in region us-west2. Compare with other experiments that used x86 builder.
- (4) Manifest creation logs show: "uploaded manifest for chkpt-20251115-04 size=104857600 sha256=3f2b..." at 02:59:01Z. Object creation time on GCS shows 02:59:12Z (11s later), but tarball size on GCS at 02:59:05Z was 0 bytes then quickly increased. Possible race.

Commands to reproduce locally (worked-ish):
- python scripts/pack_checkpoint.py --input-dir=out/epoch_10 --output=chkpt-local.tar.gz --embed-sentinel  # script used in training toolchain (I added --embed-sentinel to mimic bad builder)
- sha256sum chkpt-local.tar.gz && python -c "import tarfile; t=tarfile.open('chkpt-local.tar.gz'); print(t.getmembers()[:5])"  # tarfile can open even with sentinel if sentinel is before tar? observed different behaviour depending on sentinel length

Immediate mitigation ideas (quick):
- Add a defensive fallback in serving runtime: if header version unknown, attempt to sniff compression (zstd/gzip) and skip known sentinel prefixes (ASCII v1/v2) up to 4096 bytes and search for tar header signature. Log the original header blob to s3 for postmortem.
- In upload pipeline: add atomic manifest upload after successful checksum verification and delay manifest write until object size stabilizes for 30s or until a second read of sha256 matches.
- Block ARM builders until we validate parity of header format across architectures.

Next actionable steps (my plan):
- [ ] Add small repro tarball with embedded sentinel and upload to a staging bucket, then run serving runtime locally against it. Save exact object metadata.
- [ ] Add python snippet into runtime tests that scans first 8k bytes for tar magic and validates resilience to small ASCII prefaces.
- [ ] Open INF-4321 (was created) and attach logs + failing object path + sha256. Ping @infra-oncall and @training-team on Slack.
- [ ] Ask build team to rerun training job on x86 for a single checkpoint and compare artifacts.

Links / artifacts:
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321
- GH draft repro: https://github.com/redwoodinference/inference-runtime/pull/1234 (WIP, branch maya/checkpoint-scan)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01ABCD2EFG/p1716789200000456

Notes to self: keep this doc informal. If this turns out to be pipeline race, we likely need a small library for safe checkpoint publishing that everyone uses. If it's format drift from ARM builder, that's a one-off but we should add CI to pack/unpack across arch targets.

Raw snippets captured: (redacted)
- hexdump output (failing): 
  00000000  28 b5 2f 5d 0a 00 02 00  00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00  |(./]............|
  00000010  53 45 4e 54 49 4e 45 4c  3a 73 68 61 72 64 5f 6d  |SENTINEL:shard_m|

- runtime exception: 
  ValueError: Unsupported checkpoint header version: 0x0f  at serving/runtime/checkpoint.py:142

End of notes (will trim and paste to ticket).
